issues.description: The archive contains the datasheet and three programs but none of the CSV/DTA inputs referenced by those programs. The datasheet documents author-prepared, de-identified professional data. Ask only for compatible de-identified analysis files or a supported producer; the destroyed real-name crosswalk is historical/privacy context and is not an input required by the supplied code. A permitted shareable route remains unverified.

The supplied Stata program collapses data in memory and writes tables; it does not save fontaneros_seth_monthly.dta or fontaneros_seth_weekly.dta. It also reads fontaneros_pda.dta and fontaneros_region.dta without supplied producers. Confirm which files are intended author-prepared primary inputs and supply their compatible producer/specification and order; do not infer that Stata creates them.

The Stata program insheets and renames the preliminary CSV, then immediately replaces the in-memory data with use ..., clear; no later command uses those imported values. Because this read is active, an absent file prevents an unmodified run, but its analytical role and whether the read is obsolete must be confirmed before proposing its removal.

The Stata workflow uses the prior weekly detractor observation and monthly l2/f2 and l6/f6 operator comparisons; the R inputs contain corresponding precomputed boundary fields. Required start/end periods, continuity and preparation history are not supplied. Do not infer history from the estimation filters alone.

The Stata file defines local mypath only for Mac and Windows, with Dropbox-specific paths. No path setup for other operating systems is supplied, and the project-relative directory tree is not part of the archive.

weekly_jar.R calls replacementRegressMonthly with regType "C", but its switch alternative is named lowercase c. R matches character switch alternatives exactly; this section has no matching model branch, so the Table 4 C simulation cannot produce its intended model output. The output name uses uppercase C, so correct the switch key while preserving the model formula and filename.

The weekly script starts with dplyr/survival/VGAM/lfe but later calls makeSOCKcluster, clusterExport, clusterEvalQ, stopCluster, times and %dopar% without an explicit namespace or package attachment. doSNOW::registerDoSNOW is qualified, but does not make the other names available in a clean session. The clean-session metadata probe found none of these names; do not rely on monthly_jar.R having run first.

monthly_jar.R arms debugonce immediately before its direct regression call. The supplied setting enters the debugger, but unattended behavior depends on the R launcher and input handling: a bounded vanilla R probe with closed stdin completed the call with return code 0 while printing the debugger trace. Treat this as launcher-dependent interactive friction and an optional cleanup candidate, not an unconditional batch-run blocker.

Both R scripts write into relative results/ paths but do not create that directory. Confirm it exists and is writable in the launch working directory before running; no output folder is included in the packaged inventory.

The R simulations draw replacement treatment assignments with sample() and run 1,000 parallel repetitions without a supplied seed or parallel RNG stream setup. Exact Monte Carlo outputs have no documented deterministic replay setting. Ask whether exact seed-level matching is expected and record the authors’ intended RNG setup; do not invent a seed.

evidence.description: Main Stata DTA fields used to derive dates, month/week indices, experiment flags and outcomes.

use "stata import data post/fontaneros_detalle_post.dta" , clear

replace encuesta = "." if encuesta=="SIN VALORACION"
destring encuesta , replace

encode gremio_codigo , generate (codigo_gremio)

tostring reparacion_fin , replace
gen date_fin = date(reparacion_fin, "DM20Y")
format date_fin %d
drop mes
gen mes = month(date_fin)
drop semana2
gen semana2 = int((date_fin - td(29apr2013))/7) if date_fin >= td(29apr2013)
replace semana2 = int((date_fin - td(29apr2013))/7) -1 if date_fin < td(29apr2013)

gen experimento = 0
replace experimento = 1 if date_fin>=td(01may2013) & date_fin<td(01aug2013)
gen experimento_post = 0
replace experimento_post = 1 if date_fin>=td(01aug2013)
gen detractor = 0 if encuesta>=0 & encuesta<11
replace detractor = 1 if encuesta<7 & encuesta>=0
gen promotor = 0 if encuesta>=0 & encuesta<11
replace promotor = 1 if encuesta<11 & encuesta>=9

generate insatisfechos = 0
replace insatisfechos = 1 if insatisfecho=="S"

actions.description: Request the author-prepared, de-identified analysis files or their actual preparation programs, and clarify the CSV’s role and input history. Do not request names/official IDs or reconstruct the proprietary experiment data independently.
steps: Ask the authors for a shareable, de-identified version of the repair-level post DTA and the operator-month PDA and operator-region DTA used by Stata, with source column definitions and merge keys.

Ask for fontaneros_seth_monthly.dta and fontaneros_seth_weekly.dta or the documented programs that actually produce them; confirm their producer-consumer order because the supplied Stata file does not save those files.
Ask whether the preliminary CSV is still a required input. The current code reads and renames it, then clears it; if it is obsolete, request author confirmation before removing this no-op read.

For each file, obtain exact fields, row unit, period, key uniqueness, transformation notes and coverage. Confirm weekly prior-period history and monthly two- and six-period lead/lag history; do not use estimation end dates as coverage evidence.
